paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus is really alive, and He gave His disciples proof right in front of them. He said, "Look at My hands and My feet. It is I Myself." (Luke 24:39) Then He ate a piece of broiled fish in front of them (Luke 24:42-43). I think a Jesus who would rather prove it than argue about it is one you can trust with your own doubts.

But He didn't stop at proving it. He opened their minds to understand the Scriptures (Luke 24:45), and He told them the Christ will suffer and rise on the third day (Luke 24:46). So the cross and the empty tomb were never a surprise, because it was all written about Him in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms (Luke 24:44). That's why we keep opening the Word, baker, because it's all pointing to Him, and He's the One who helps us understand it.

And then He gave them a job: "You are witnesses of these things." (Luke 24:48) Repentance and forgiveness of sins would be proclaimed in His name to all nations, and He told them to wait for power from on high before they started (Luke 24:47, 49). Look where they ended up: worshiping Him with great joy and praising God continually in the temple (Luke 24:52-53). Their doubts and fear turned into worship, friend, and I think that's a good reason to bring Him yours.
